name: non-oxidative propane dehydrogenation

sources.propane_usd_t: EIA Mont Belvieu propane spot 2024 0.778 USD/gal at 4.2 lb/gal = 408 USD/t
sources.reference X, S: Oleflex: 86 % selectivity at 40 % single-pass conversion (Dong, Altvater, Mark, Hermans, OSTI 1866245, p17); propane use 1.2 lb per lb propylene (PetroLogistics SEC 424B4 2012) = S 0.873
sources.reference T: Oleflex 525-705 C, 1-3 bar (Moffat PhD thesis, Glasgow 2023, p5); 640 C and 1.5 bar chosen inside that window
sources.h2_ratio: assumption (not found in an open source)
sources.t_cycle_h: Oleflex CCR cycle 5-8 days (Dong et al. p17): 6.5 d
sources.catalyst_life_y: reactor catalyst replaced about every three years (PetroLogistics SEC 424B4)
sources.capex: 1.30 bn USD (Dec 2012) for 1.654 bn lb/y = 750 kt/y, annualised at 7 %, 20 y (Enterprise Products PDH, EPA GHG permit application)
sources.e_proc_GJ_per_t_feed: calibrated so that the reference plant buys 17.5 GJ natural gas per t propylene after burning its own H2 and light ends (PetroLogistics: 9.96 M MMBtu for ~601 kt propylene)
sources.power_kWh_per_t_feed: calibrated to PetroLogistics fuel + utilities 35.4 M USD/y minus gas 25.9 M USD/y = ~16 USD/t propylene at 0.08 USD/kWh
sources.reference r, Pt 0.3 wt%, Sn 0.3 wt%: assumption (Oleflex Pt loading not in an open source; '<1 wt%' search summary only)
sources.thermo: dH298 124.3 kJ/mol (Moffat Eq. 1); equilibrium fit as noted

common_notes: crf 0.0944 = 7 %/y over 20 y (Enterprise Products PDH, EPA GHG permit application 2012). gas 2.5 USD/GJ = 2.60 USD/MMBtu paid by the PetroLogistics Catofin plant (SEC 424B4, 2012); Henry Hub 2024 2.19 USD/MMBtu (EIA). fixed O&M 4 %/y of capex, power 0.08 USD/kWh, metal recovery 0.95 and financing 0.08/y: assumptions as in the NH3/methanol chains.
